references.text: Moses gave the territory on the east side of the Jordan to the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh, confirming the distribution mentioned in Joshua 13:8.
The sons of Reuben and Gad asked Moses for the land east of the Jordan as their inheritance, which is the background for the land allocation described in Joshua 13:8.
Moses describes how he gave the land east of the Jordan to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh, corresponding to the inheritance mentioned in Joshua 13:8.
Moses reminds them that they took the land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh, in agreement with Joshua 13:8.
Joshua reminds the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh that Moses gave them land east of the Jordan, referring to the same inheritance as in Joshua 13:8.
The text tells how Moses and the Israelites defeated the kings east of the Jordan, and Moses gave this land to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
Joshua sends the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh back to their inheritance that Moses had given them on the east side of the Jordan.
Confirmation that the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh had already received their inheritance on the east side of the Jordan.
